title: AI Product Video Prompts: 8 Shots for Product Photos
summary: Copy eight AI product-video prompts for bottles, shoes, food, and furniture. Choose a source photo, direct one shot, and check product fidelity before export.
body_markdown:
Turn a product photo into a short video by asking for one camera move or one small environmental change while keeping the product recognizable. Start with a locked-camera shot when labels or fine details matter. Below are eight copyable image-to-video prompts, the source photo each needs, and the defects to check before using the result.


Open[Magic Hour Image-to-Video](https://magichour.ai/products/image-to-video) , upload your own product photo, and paste one prompt below. Select duration, aspect ratio, and an available model in the tool. The prompts are starting points to adapt; the cover is an editorial illustration, not a set of measured model outputs.

## 1. Locked camera and moving light


**Use for:** packaging where the front label must remain recognizable. Start with an evenly lit photo in which the full label is legible.


**Prompt to copy:** Keep the camera fixed on the product in the uploaded photo. The product remains completely still in its original position. A soft studio highlight moves slowly across the background. Preserve the product's silhouette, label lettering, cap, color, and contact shadow. One continuous shot with calm, restrained motion.


**Check:** compare the label at the beginning, middle, and end. If lettering changes, keep the real product photo as a fixed layer in your editor and animate the background separately.


## 2. Gentle product push-in


**Use for:** a simple hero shot of a bottle, jar, or box. Leave room around the product so the closer framing does not cut it off.


**Prompt to copy:** Use the uploaded product photo as the starting frame. The camera makes a very slow, small push toward the stationary product. Keep the entire product visible throughout the shot. Preserve its proportions, label, surface finish, color, and placement. The existing background and lighting stay consistent. A single smooth shot.


**Check:** watch for a cap changing size, a label bending, or the object growing independently of the camera move. Reduce movement if these appear.


## 3. Sideways slide for shoes and accessories


**Use for:** a side-view product image with space on both sides. This prompt requests a small change in viewpoint, not a full rotation.


**Prompt to copy:** The camera slides a short distance to the right, moving slowly and parallel to the product in the uploaded image. The product remains stationary. Keep its visible shape, stitching, edges, material, and colors consistent. Maintain the original lighting and surface. Finish while the same side of the product is still visible.


**Check:** inspect laces, straps, handles, and the sole or base. A single photo cannot establish what the hidden side of a real product looks like. Use additional real views or filmed footage for a full rotation.


## 4. Material and texture detail


**Use for:** an existing close-up of fabric, leather, wood, or another material. The source needs enough detail for the area you want to show.


**Prompt to copy:** Begin with the uploaded close-up. Move the camera very slowly along the visible material, maintaining the same angle and distance. Keep the original weave or grain, seams, surface texture, and color consistent. Soft, steady lighting. Show a restrained detail shot of the existing surface.


**Check:** reject invented seams, changing grain, or texture that looks like a different material. Generation does not verify the product's actual construction.


## 5. Steam above a still drink or dish


**Use for:** a photograph of a product that is genuinely served hot. Avoid this treatment if it would misrepresent the item.


**Prompt to copy:** Keep the cup or dish and every visible ingredient in the uploaded photo still and unchanged. The camera remains fixed. A small amount of delicate steam rises slowly above the hot product and fades naturally. Preserve the container, label, food shape, portion size, lighting, and background.


**Check:** the steam should be the change. Reject extra ingredients, a moving logo, a melting container, or a different portion. Use the clip to illustrate presentation, not to prove a product claim.


## 6. Small furniture pull-back


**Use for:** furniture already photographed in a room with enough surrounding space. A tight crop gives the model little evidence about the wider scene.


**Prompt to copy:** Start from the uploaded room photograph. The camera pulls back slightly and slowly while keeping the furniture centered. Preserve the furniture's dimensions, upholstery, legs, corners, and position in the room. Maintain the visible room layout, lighting, and perspective. One continuous, stable shot.


**Check:** compare leg count, straight edges, scale, and nearby objects. If the move reveals invented room details, use a wider source image or a fixed-camera shot.


## 7. Move the background, hold the product


**Use for:** a product with a simple background and a clean outline. Name the exact background element that should move.


**Prompt to copy:** The product in the uploaded photo stays fixed in the foreground. Only the soft out-of-focus light in the background shifts gently. Keep the camera still and preserve the product's label, outline, color, material, and contact shadow. The product remains the clear focal point throughout.


**Check:** inspect the outline and translucent surfaces for background changes bleeding into the product. For strict packaging fidelity, compositing the original product over a separately animated background gives you direct control over that layer.


## 8. End-card hold with space for copy


**Use for:** a photo already composed with empty space beside or above the product. Add your final price, offer, and call to action in an editor after generation.


**Prompt to copy:** Hold the composition of the uploaded photo. The product remains still, fully visible, and unchanged. Keep the existing empty space clear. Use only subtle background light movement, then settle into a calm final hold. Preserve all product details and the original framing throughout the shot.


**Check:** make sure the generated motion leaves enough stable space for your message. Add readable text yourself rather than depending on generated lettering for an offer or legal disclosure.


## Turn three shots into a simple product video


Use one establishing shot, one detail shot, and one end-card hold. For example: show a shoe with the sideways slide, show its material using a real close-up, then finish with the original product composition and a clear next step. Assemble the accepted clips in your video editor. Reuse the same product references so the shots describe the same item.


For the spoken message or on-screen sequence, choose a[product-video script template](https://magichour.ai/blog/product-video-script-templates) . For choosing the source image, use the[reference-image workflow](https://magichour.ai/blog/how-to-use-reference-images-in-image-to-video) . These solve different parts of the job: the script determines what you communicate; the shot prompt requests how an image moves.


## The five checks before export


- **Identity:** shape, label, color, material, and visible features still match the real product.
- **Continuity:** inspect the whole clip for flicker, morphing, duplicate parts, and sudden camera changes.
- **Truthfulness:** the video does not invent a product function, ingredient, included accessory, or observed result.
- **Delivery:** the crop, readable copy, audio, and export match the destination's requirements.
- **Cost:** include rejected completed generations and editing time when comparing usable-output cost. Use the[video-cost worksheet](https://magichour.ai/blog/ai-video-pricing-index) .


## Do these prompts work with every model?


They describe a shot rather than an API request, so you can adapt them to an image-to-video interface that accepts an image and a text prompt. Results, controls, and supported inputs differ by model and provider. Follow the selected tool's documented settings; writing a duration or resolution in the prompt does not change the actual output setting.


Magic Hour's[model reference](https://docs.magichour.ai/api-reference/models) documents supported output options. Runway's[camera-direction guide](https://runway.com/resources/ai-camera-prompts) explains common camera terms. Product access and source links were checked September 9, 2026.


## What if the product must match perfectly?


Keep the real product photograph or filmed product as a fixed source layer and use AI for surrounding motion where appropriate. Inspect the composite too. A prompt asking for an unchanged label is a request to the model, not a guarantee of exact preservation.


To try one of these shots,[upload a product photo to Magic Hour Image-to-Video](https://magichour.ai/products/image-to-video) and start with the simplest movement that serves your message.
